content: Upper respiratory tract infection is a condition caused by an acute infection that affects the upper respiratory tract, including the nose, sinuses, pharynx, or larynx. In the United States, there are approximately one billion cases of acute upper respiratory illnesses each year. About 15% of acute pharyngitis cases are caused by bacterial infections, most commonly by Group A Streptococcus, which is also known as Strep Throat. Patients with Strep Throat typically experience a sore throat as their initial symptom. Unlike viral upper respiratory infections, they usually do not present with symptoms such as a runny nose, cough, or sneezing. Upper respiratory tract infections are highly prevalent, with an estimated one billion cases occurring annually in the United States alone. While anyone can develop a common cold or upper respiratory tract infection, certain populations are more susceptible. These include children, elderly individuals, and those with weakened immune systems.
